title: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

sense.text: “But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.” Christ spoke this to the disciples, but in these last days it speaks to us, because we build on the foundation of Christ and the apostles, and move as able ministers of the New Testament.

“Many prophets and righteous men have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them.” Our forefathers could not fully understand the things they were shown, so they explained them the best they could. When they spoke of a serpent whose power was all in its head, they didn’t know what the hell a missile was. Now we see those things, and that is a blessing.

The Most High has put his spirit on our leaders to explain it and show it to us, and we have the capacity to understand it, not just to hear it and say wow. But for some it is only entertainment, because it doesn’t move them to correction or to urgency. Prophecy should move us to correction. As we see these things unfold in the last days, they should push us to do our self-assessments, and if you really are moved by prophecy, you should be moved to action by what the scripture says.

World events are never random. The Most High’s hand is down here, his eyes are always upon us, and the nations are under his control, even when something seems wild: “the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men.”

So when war rises and alliances shift, scripture already told us it would happen, and that the basest of men would lead. Trump says it out of the beast’s own mouth: nothing can stop him but his own morality and his own mind, and he doesn’t need international law. By what we just read, his is the basest mind.

“See that ye be not troubled.” We don’t sleep as others do. Like a team moving down the field ten yards at a time toward the goal, we see ourselves moving forward when these things happen, so it is not a time of worry for us. It should be a worry only if you are not in the right spirit to move with urgency to repent. “For all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.”

“Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places.” We have had the food shortages and the prices up, COVID and different diseases, and some among the body who were touched by COVID the Lord received. All these things happen, and still the end is not yet.
“All these are the beginning of sorrows”, and it has been going on for a long time.

“Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you.” Jacob’s trouble is not here yet. Are we being delivered up? Are we being killed? Not yet. That can escalate quickly on the Lord’s timeline, and we don’t know when it will be, but all these other things must happen first, then the next move: “ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.”

precepts.why:
Ezra shows the nations rising together: “the nations of the dragons of Arabia shall come out with many chariots, and the multitude of them shall be carried as the wind upon earth, that all they which hear them may fear and tremble.” That is the Arabs, Ishmael, the wild men.

“Also the Carmanians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood”: the Carmanians are Iran, which prophecy puts at the centerpiece of it all. “And with great power shall they come, and join battle with them”, with the Arab nations, “and shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians”, over on that side of the earth. Wasting a portion deals with nukes, and it deals with unity, Iran and the Arabs together.

Right now none of those things are present. What we are seeing are contractions. There are certain steps that have to happen for them to be united with each other, and that is the stage being set.

“And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved.” Things will get so crazy in the earth that the Lord moves the events forward. Shortened means the events accelerate.

That is the similitude of a woman in travail: times of contraction, then a time of relief from it, but every contraction means you are being inched closer, another ten yards down the field. It is an acceleration of events, just as the prophets described. What we are witnessing is extremely significant, the days being shortened, and we shouldn’t sleep on it. Do not think what is happening over there is insignificant by any measure. It may seem far off, but the Lord can put spirit on men to move things along quicker and increase the speed of those events.

sense.text: “Of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you”: it doesn’t need to be explained to us; we should know this already.

“The day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night.” Throughout all of history, every time something happened on a global scale, our people asked, is this the time? They asked whether he would now restore the kingdom; in Matthew 24 they asked when these things would happen. We were always watching for it, and Christ always gave us the sign, but not with dates and times, because much of it depends on when we are sealed, when the 144 and all the other pieces are in place.

Read on in the chapter and it speaks of us not sleeping, being alert, aware and sober-minded. To be sober takes action. It takes abstinence: abstinence from sin.
“Wherefore comfort yourselves together, and edify one another, even as also ye do.” Knowing all these things, we don’t comfort ourselves with hugs and kisses. We edify one another.

“Warn them that are unruly”: those that don’t want to follow what the Bible says, as many do with marriage. “Comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, be patient toward all men.” In these verses is the whole ministry we must focus on.

“See that none render evil for evil unto any man; but ever follow that which is good.” “For this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.” It is God’s will that we do these things. As we see these times and these things happening, these are the moments to move forward.

“Quench not the Spirit. Despise not prophesyings. Prove all things; hold fast that which is good. Abstain from all appearance of evil.” Prophecy is not meant to entertain us. It is meant to correct us. The more we see the signs, the more urgently we should be repenting, correcting our lives and strengthening our households to prepare for those days. How are you going to do in that day, in the afflictions that are coming, when there are still issues in the marriages and divisions, and you can’t even endure each other? We have to band together in those times.

If the days truly are getting shorter, and they are, then marriage, family order and the structure of the household can’t be treated casually anymore. Marriage is the foundation of nation building. If the marriages and the households are weak, and your household could be yourself alone, then how are you going to stand in that wicked day? We have to get it right according to scripture, and we have to get it right now.

Marriage didn’t originate with romance, culture or society. Before there were governments or ceremonies, God joined man and woman together in Eden. Outside of sanctifying the seventh day, the union of man and wife is the first institution God ordained. That is how important marriage is, and it is the first thing Satan attacked. Through the process of time man sought out many inventions, and most of what we now think marriage is, is man-made. Most enter it with expectations formed by the world, not by scripture, and that is why so many marriages struggle, including among ourselves.

The Lord God took the rib from Adam, made a woman, “and brought her unto the man.” This is marriage. There was no feast at the first marriage; it was the ordaining of the union.

It starts with order and authority. The woman was taken from the man, and that was no random thing. Artwork shows a spiritual hand forming both the man and the woman out of the dust of the ground, and that is the same BS as Eve biting an apple and handing it to Adam: subtle things to warp your understanding, and a lie spoken often enough becomes the truth without validation. Man and woman were made very differently. The breath of life was breathed into the man, but not into the woman, because that was the man’s authority and the man’s responsibility. God was setting order when he did the marriage.

“This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.” Magnify what is being said here and it is where all the classic vows came from: in sickness and in health, for better or worse, till death do us part. But the real vows are what is read in Tobit 8. People who write their own vows write some wild stuff, further and further from what God ordained.

“Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.” One flesh has many layers, spiritual ones, but here it means inseparable. That doesn’t mean you’re up your wife’s skirt all the time, best friend, best friend. You can be close with your spouse, but men have priorities that God has given them, and an order to them: without God there is no wife and no family. If you abandon God and his mission, the rest of it can be touched.

In the first marriage recorded in scripture there is no courtship, no attraction language, no emotional decision-making. God forms the woman and brings her to the man. Marriage began as a divine institution, not a human invention, designed to run by God’s order from the beginning; what we call marriage today is a human invention.

precepts.why:
Behind the union is a covenant, and a covenant is a contract. You understand the damn contract for your phone plan, your job or a sports deal, but something as powerful and profound as marriage you don’t.

“Because the Lord hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth.” God did the first marriage, and God is in the midst of every marriage: what God has joined together, let no man put asunder. The world kept rudiments of it, asking whether there are any objections and pronouncing man and wife before the Lord and the witnesses, but rudiments are only a part, not the whole.

“Against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion.” If you are being treacherous with your wife, or with your husband, that is still your companion; you are one flesh. “And the wife of thy covenant”: of the contract you made.

A covenant is not based on feelings. Sign a contract on feelings, like buying a car because you like the smell and the color, and you get ripped on the interest rate and the add-ons. Some brothers marry that way: I’ll deal with all this because she bad. She ain’t going to be bad forever. Men age gracefully, women just age, and when the hormones change you have to be able to live with that person, through every dinner, every drive, every wake-up. It has to be stronger than romance and attraction. Covenants are built on commitment and obligation.

Modern ideas of marriage assume feelings are the foundation: find the love of your life, find your prince charming. Men are much more realistic and pliable in dealing with it, because the spirit of life was breathed into the man; for the sake of honour, men will most of the time do what is right just because it is in their makeup. Women in general are so driven by feelings that they will justify doing something wrong to stand on them. We look at women and think soft, but from women came the beginning of sin; principally they are the more immoral, if the scriptures are not keeping them right. Eve is the mother of all, and as is the mother, so is the daughter: it is in your genetic makeup, and it only needs the right nudge to bring it out.

sense.text:
Marriage among the forefathers was not built on romance as its foundation. Romance comes from the Latin Romanus, Rome: it is a Roman custom, carried on through the chivalry of the knights of France in the Middle Ages. It is about passion and attraction, putting feelings over practical concerns, even absent a commitment, and it ends more often in disappointment. Sisters, you want the love story, but a love story not based on God, when you could have the love story the scripture gives, with all those things and more, and eternal life and the glory of the kingdom after it as joint heirs together.

What TV sells is a lie: Friends and Sex in the City, young people in big New York apartments sitting over coffee, three or four vacations a year. That lie goes in your head, and when the marriage is the supermarket and dinner at home, she is depressed and in her feelings: this isn’t what I thought it would be. I’m not responsible for your expectations. That is why proving matters: talk about what life you expect and how you see marriage, and look for a woman that talks about support for the mission, building the family, and finding joy in the everyday. Some sisters will try to game you with that, but Adam saw past Eve’s BS and did it anyway to please her; it is up to you whether you give that water passage.

Many only get married because they want sex, which is the only way it is lawful and not fornication, but they still carry the expectations of the world: a warm body and maybe the extra income. Don’t ever get with somebody for extra income. In ancient times that was never a motive, because the man provided everything. Knowing how evil and wicked the Romans are, that alone should get you off it. And a sister who wants her king to serve her makes no sense; a king governs and provides for his people, he doesn’t take orders.

“Abram and Nahor took them wives.” There is no attraction language here. Not that they weren’t attracted, and not to go marry someone fugly, but it was not given the importance we give it now. Women are more trivial about it, and it goes into hypergamy: men traditionally date down and then marry who they are with if she provides what they need, while women hold to standards like five foot ten and won’t give a brother the time of day. If your type is about appearance and not character, examine where your head is.

And what follows immediately? They moved. Sarai didn’t buck up against going to another country; they shared the risk and the hardship as a family. Terah took his son, his grandson and his daughter in law: you married a whole family. You don’t think about everything that comes with it when you’re thinking of romance. None of the righteous forefathers and foremothers had an issue with these movements.

Partnership and intimacy come later, as the marriage progresses and you age together. Expecting them outright from the beginning is backwards.

“And she became his wife; and he loved her.” She became his wife, then he loved her. It doesn’t say he loved her before. Brothers three months into proving saying I love her, I think I love her: that is usually mommy issues. There is no love at first sight here. What we call love at first sight is really lust at first sight, and whenever that is the primary mover, disorder comes behind it.

God ordained this; he lined them up to be together. And these are only the forefathers scripture highlights. Consider the millions of other Israelites and how their marriages were made.

precepts.why:
Here is how it developed later: “when he had been there a long time”, Abimelech king of the Philistines “looked out at a window, and saw, and, behold, Isaac was sporting with Rebekah his wife.” The partnership and the intimacy came after.

Intimacy is not just sex, just as lust is not just sex. Intimacy is the comfort to be the truest form of yourself in front of your spouse. A man has to keep a balance and keep order, but your spouse will see more of you than anybody else ever will. Sporting together means Abimelech probably saw them laughing and having a good time.

Those things come later, not before. The lead-up to their marriage never says they were doing that beforehand. Some want it now, like the brother sitting knee to knee with a sister to feel the electricity, or taking her out to eat. What is driving that is hormones, and everything gets clouded: you start to rationalize, I’ll overlook this, I’ll overlook that. It is much more clean and structured than that.

sense.text:
This is the first time scripture really speaks of attraction between the betrothed. Attraction is present; scripture speaks of making a covenant with your eyes because what you see first is what appeals to you. But then you have to put that down and get your spiritual eyes and your spiritual mind on.

Why is this in the Bible? When Jacob saw Rachel, he thought she was such a baddie that he rolled up his sleeves, “rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the flock”: flexing his muscles, like the birds on the nature shows puffing their chests and showing their colors in a mating ritual. Instead of focusing on the rock, did she see me? Notice how it altered his behavior already. Abram moved and went about God’s business; Isaac had his directives and built a foundation and a marriage. Jacob over here losing his mind over Rachel.
“And Jacob kissed Rachel”: it was a greeting, not making out, like the little kiss on the cheek the Northern Kingdom would give in the world.

“Leah was tender eyed; but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured. And Jacob loved Rachel.” See the contrast: Isaac married Rebekah, consummated it, then loved her. Jacob loved her already. When you build things on attraction, you don’t have your right senses in place. He lost his damn mind.

“And they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her.” We read love and think it is something pure, but what was it based on? What he saw. What is emphasized here is physical beauty, emotional attraction and romantic motivation. There was no word for romance back then, but he was romantically motivated.

And what came of it? Deception in the marriage, competition, and family tension, with Leah, Rachel and even handmaids in the mix. When something is romance driven, scripture doesn’t hide the cost. It documents it.

Physical attraction leads to problems. At first it sounds romantic: Shechem saw her and was enamored. But “he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.” When you do things with your eyes, what drives it is evil intent, because you forget everything else.

“And he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel.” The love comes after the violation, when there was an order and a custom for how those things should be. What came of it was more deception, the slaughter of the men of Shechem, and turmoil in Jacob’s house. Visual attraction produced violence and bloodshed, and you see it all the time: jealousy, killing, all types of madness. It’s not that you can’t be attracted to someone. We put too much emphasis on the attraction.
Samson saw “a woman in Timnath of the daughters of the Philistines”, and told his father and mother, “now therefore get her for me to wife.” She bad. I got to have her.

“Is there never a woman among the daughters of thy brethren, or among all my people”: it is like Tobit’s word to marry of thy kindred. He wanted to marry of the other nations, because she was bad and he lost his mind. “Get her for me; for she pleaseth me well.” He felt it in his loins, the electricity in his pee-pee, and he didn’t care what he was supposed to look for. That’s like the brother who sees nothing he likes in his congregation and goes to another city or online to grab one up, and sisters do it too, hoping the person will understand all this later. It’s all types of deception and madness when it comes from attraction alone, like the brother who found a baddie online and it was a dude.

His reasoning was purely visual. What came of it was conflict with the Philistines, betrayal, the death of thirty men, and escalation into full war. In Judges 16 his attraction cost him his vow and his strength: his eyes gouged out and enslavement, all because she made the peepee tingle. It is a cautionary tale that men should not move that way, because you give up your preeminence and your strength. Attraction is the gateway to destruction if that’s the only thing you’re moving on.

“And the woman was very beautiful to look upon”: there is the visual attraction again. He saw her, he inquired, and he took her, the same pattern as Shechem. What came of it was adultery, the murder of Uriah, a national scandal, the death of the child, and long-term chaos in David’s house. The Lord forgave him but left him with drama the rest of his days. One fleeting moment of attraction, happening to walk up on the roof, and generational consequences after it.

You take chess and spades seriously and see moves ahead, but not marriage: ah, she look good, I got to marry her so I can have her.

“There was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.” Beauty became part of Absalom’s identity, his hair and his physical perfection, and what came behind it was ambition and rebellion. You get a big head about yourself. He rebelled against his father, there was civil war, and he died hanging from that very hair, the thing that was vanity to him. Whenever physical attraction becomes the forefront of anything, the Bible shows that trouble comes behind it.

This is why the scripture says these things: “Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” Not in your heart and not in your mind. She gives you the look back, you make the eye contact, you feel the chemistry, the sparks fly, and you done lost your mind: I got to have her.

precepts.why:
“And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.” There is the physical again: the attire, and the subtle heart, to entice. And it works; you fall for it. Solomon warns of being captured by appearance, and he knew, having dealt with a thousand women. It shows how intoxicating it can be.

The pattern is the same every time. Shechem saw her and took her, and violence and massacre followed. Samson, she pleased him well, and betrayal and blindness. David saw her beauty and had to have her, and adultery and murder. Absalom was celebrated for his own beauty, and pride and rebellion. Strange women being beautiful leads to ruin. Adam and Eve show creation and order; Abraham and Sarah, covenant and mission; Isaac and Rebekah, ordained, and the love came after; Jacob and Rachel, attraction and complication. The Bible doesn’t deny attraction; it is just not the foundation.

So the Bible rarely describes the beauty of wives. Leah was tender eyed; they weren’t all dime pieces. Of Rebekah it tells her character, her hospitality and her faith, her actions more than her appearance. Zipporah’s beauty is never described, and Elizabeth is called righteous, not beautiful. What is highlighted among the foremothers is righteousness, obedience, wisdom and faith. The beauty of a woman is in the ordering of her house. The virtuous woman’s price is far above rubies not because she’s a baddie but for her virtue and her submission to her lord, which shows her submission to God. A ten physically who is a one as a person don’t work.

The world glorifies women from the womb, and social media validates them with likes, clicks and looks, and it raises a subtle spirit of vanity. Don’t walk out your house like a bum; appearance matters as far as being presentable. But some put too much status on it, especially women.

sense.text: What should we be focused on? Tobias, shut in with his wife, rises first to pray: “Sister, arise, and let us pray that God would have pity on us.” His prayer shows the example he learned from the lessons of Tobit, and in these brief words it speaks volumes about his understanding of marriage. Married or unmarried, meditate on these verses. Don’t let the words of power just fall; embrace each word and let it soak in.

“Thou madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay”: that is the foundation, brothers and sisters. Do it right: if you haven’t proven for three years and you want Deacon Yashua to do your wedding, he is not doing it. “Of them came mankind”: a nation, the abundance of people. Marriage is nation building.

“I take not this my sister for lust, but uprightly”: not for attraction’s sake, not for romance. He already said in his prayer why he takes her. “Therefore mercifully ordain that we may become aged together.” Aged together is the long, intertwined journey of growing old side by side: a shared history, mutual support through life’s changes, a deep committed bond that accepts the aging and faces life’s challenges as a team. Aged means refined, the way you age wine and cheese.

That is where the love and everything else grows, after. With age comes beauty, love and passion: the enchantment, the strengthening of the relationship, not whimsical BS out of a movie. Everything else has to be established first, or the romance will be fleeting and break the foundation of the scriptures. Stop chasing a feeling. Stop chasing an emotion. Get your mind like Tobias’ mind, and your household and your marriage will be stronger, your children the outcome of it, and us as a people by extension, stronger for the time of troubles to come.
“And she said with him, Amen.” She agreed, because her mind is of her lord. She didn’t ask, wait, what about the house, what about the gifts, none of the things the world talks about.

precepts.why:
There’s your romance: “Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest”. Living joyfully is part of the aging together. “All the days of the life of thy vanity”, because we are here only a fleeting moment, seventy or eighty years at best. All the days God gives you, you should live joyfully with your wife; that is a commandment.

“For that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.” That is how things are supposed to be set up. If you want to navigate this world the right way, you have to navigate the marriage this way.

“Let thy fountain be blessed: and rejoice with the wife of thy youth. Let her be as the loving hind and pleasant roe”: you want passion in the relationship? Here. “Let her breasts satisfy thee at all times; and be thou ravished always with her love.” To be ravished is to be filled with intense delight and rapture: delight, charm, enthrall, captivate, spellbind, bewitch, fascinate. That goes into the power a woman has in her voice and her conversation.

There is your passion and your romance, after the foundation of the marriage is set up correctly and you age together. It can’t exist if the other divine parts of the marriage are not set up right. You don’t seek this first. It’s like picking out the furniture, the pictures for the wall and the rugs before you’ve even bought the house, not knowing whether the walls will hold or the foundation is strong. That is how marriage is treated nowadays.

sense.text: Sirach gives more insight into the character that strengthens a marriage. “A man and a wife that agree together” stand up beautiful before God and men. The agreement is this: she agrees to follow the scriptures that pertain to her as a wife, with no contingencies, because the Bible gives no contingencies for a wife’s behavior; you do or you don’t. And he agrees to do the same as a husband. You agree in God that you will follow his order of marriage. It is not that you both like the same music, colors and food; that is part of the aging. When each runs the marriage with their responsibilities the way the Bible says, that is beautiful in God’s eyes, because it will work the way he intended.

precepts.why: “Blessed is the man that hath a virtuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double.” Virtuous deals with her character. Everything in the marriage gets better when the wife is moving in that spirit. A virtuous wife brings peace.

“A woman that honoureth her husband shall be judged wise of all”: she honours him by agreeing to follow what the Lord says. A woman that honours her husband, that is wisdom for the woman. “But she that dishonoureth him in her pride shall be counted ungodly of all”, and pride is what fights the submission.

Honouring him is not what you think; measure yourself against the scripture: am I fulfilling all these things? When it says to teach them to love their husbands, we read it on the surface as emotion. A man experiences love through respect. That’s why he likes being around the brothers: he is respected among his peers. Respect is the chief love language of a man. If the wife reverences him, he’ll feel the love, and everything else falls into place behind it.

Not forced respect, and not submission put on for show. If you have to remember to respect your husband, you’re not in submission. If you truly desire your husband and see him as he is, not through your warped worldly view of him, it comes naturally, with no trying behind it, and watch what comes out of him innately.

“He that getteth a wife beginneth a possession, a help like unto himself, and a pillar of rest.” Marriage is partnership and support, plain and simple, not a rom-com, a novella or a soap opera. It is stability and wisdom over emotional intensity. We have to stop emphasizing the wrong thing; the emotional intensity comes as a byproduct of those things.

sense.text:
Once marriage moved away from the way the Bible set it up, society added to it, and much of what is believed essential to getting married is not found in scripture. Kneeling to propose comes from medieval chivalry, knights kneeling before lords and noble women: it symbolizes servitude and submission. Who submits to who? The wife to the husband. Those who got married before this truth and knelt: suckers. The Bible shows men taking a wife, not proposing on one knee. The engagement ring is a Roman custom, a sign of ownership and a contract between families, and the diamond became the expectation only in 1947, when De Beers sold diamonds are forever and two months’ salary. The wedding ring is Egyptian, made a sacrament later by the Catholic Church. The Bible never commands or describes wedding rings.

The white wedding dress is said to stand for purity, but it came from Queen Victoria’s wedding in 1840: white was expensive and hard to keep, a sign of money and status, a royal fashion trend. Before that brides wore their best dress, blue, red, gold or black. Scripture shows otherwise: “she had a garment of divers colours upon her: for with such robes were the king’s daughters that were virgins apparelled.” The garment was not white. Divers colours were the attire of purity.

precepts.why:
“The king’s daughter is all glorious within: her clothing is of wrought gold. She shall be brought unto the king in raiment of needlework.” It wasn’t some plain white thing. It was ornate, wrought with gold, with designs and patterns on it, and the many colors are what made it biblical.

We have the feasts and you wear something, but the worldly traditions and how this stuff is set up have to come out of your mind. Ancient weddings were agreement between families, a celebration and a marriage feast, with no industry behind them. Now the jewelry, the dresses, the venue, photography, catering, decorations, the bachelor party, the rehearsal dinner and the DJ make the wedding a multi-billion dollar industry: seventy-five thousand dollars for a package, money that could be a down payment on a house or seed money for a business.

Then the covenant of marriage becomes a wedding event, people get married for the event, and they spend more time planning the party than preparing for a lifelong marriage. If it was really about being together, you would just go and do it.

sense.text:
The honeymoon comes from fifth-century European and Norse custom: newlyweds drank mead, fermented honey, for a whole moon cycle for fertility and good fortune, a month drunk, and the name itself implies the love would wane like the moon. And it does, when it isn’t built on the foundation of marriage: the honeymoon phase is over, then you hate each other.

The Bible speaks of the first year differently: “he shall not go out to war, neither shall he be charged with any business: but he shall be free at home one year, and shall cheer up his wife which he hath taken.” Not a honeymoon vacation, but a year of responsibility to establish the household. Sent off to war, he would not create stability or bring down seed to continue his name. He wasn’t burdened with public duties so that he could establish the house. To cheer up his wife means to build the marriage, establish the household and stabilize the family, not to cheer her up with a cruise. It wasn’t recreational. In the Bible it had a purpose.

precepts.why:
“What man is there that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her? let him go and return unto his house, lest he die in the battle, and another man take her.” It was always about establishing the household, never about a vacation.

The honeymoon says vacation; the Bible says stay home. The honeymoon says romantic escape; the Bible says establish the household. Modern culture makes it an experience to have; the Bible makes it a responsibility. God gave the newly married time to build their life together, not to escape from it. Many, when there is turmoil in the house, take the wife on a vacation or a date, and for the moment pretend nothing is wrong; but the elephant in the room is never addressed, and the problems come back. One brother would take his wife on a fancy vacation every time something happened, rewarding her bad behaviour; recently she broke through the window, ninja’d through it and snuffed him, and he had to call the cops.

If marriage came from God, why do most learn about it from movies instead of scripture? Culture defines it by romance; scripture defines it by responsibility. The wedding lasts a day and the marriage a lifetime, yet people spend more time preparing for the wedding. The Bible defines marriage by covenant and the responsibility that comes with it; culture makes it about ceremony and romance.

sense.text:
Before a man takes on the care of a spouse and a household, he must be in a good space with himself: able to discipline his own emotions and process them, and to help others through theirs. Otherwise he blows up on others, or separates himself and stays away: babies, not well adjusted, not manly at all. Choosing a partner is choosing a whole lifestyle, their habits and their version of every Tuesday, for the rest of your life, and you can’t expect to change it.

Husbands are responsible for provision, leadership, instruction, and to show honour in the household to the wife and the children. “Her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish”: he has to provide for his wife’s basic needs.

precepts.why:
“But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.” That is how bad the Lord sees it.

When hard times come, the woman may hold it down for a while, as in Tobit, where she took women’s work to support the household. But Tobit didn’t say, since you’re working I’m going to play around and figure out what I want to be when I grow up. Brothers have destabilized whole households economically, quitting work because they’re not happy and playing around because the wife makes good money: risks they could never take by themselves, taken now with more lives on the line.

sense.text: Ephesians 5 describes the husband’s role as sacrificial leadership: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.”
“Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it.” It’s a sacrificial relationship.

precepts.why: “Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel.” The knowledge and the honour you give is the commitment to play your role as a husband in all matters: not complaining that this is the wife you were given, not hating her, because no man ever hated his own flesh, but dealing with the situation.

sense.text: “The just man walketh in his integrity.” Integrity is doing what’s right when nobody is looking, when nobody is there to hold you accountable, as Paul said, not in my presence only. Most men have a moral thing in us, and the just man moves with integrity in how he manages and steers his household and in everything he does as a man of God. “His children are blessed after him”, because he raised a stable, sound household to build up the family.

precepts.why: The other purpose of marriage: “Be fruitful, and multiply.” Marriage is nation building, and that means having children if you are able. That may not be what the Lord has for you in this lifetime, but children come from marriage.

Psalms 127 explains why. “Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it.” The house is the house of marriage, and by extension Israel as a people. This is why it must be handled right: let the world build the house, and you get what we have repeatedly gotten as a people.

“It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows.” Why put yourself in a situation and then cry woe is me, miserable in your marriage, full of sorrows, as though you had no power or authority and no God on your side to fix it?

He is speaking of building a house, and then of children; he didn’t change the subject at random. “Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord: and the fruit of the womb is his reward”, its own reward, because that is how we carry on. “As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth”: if the just man walks in his integrity, his children are in good condition. “Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them: they shall not be ashamed”, because you raised them godly as Sirach teaches, not only by what you told them but by what they saw in you. “But they shall speak with the enemies in the gate”: they will follow behind you and fill your shoes, pointing out the evils of our oppressors and of our people, and giving them the hope of salvation they know not. That is why his children are blessed after him.

This is integrity: “choose you this day whom ye will serve”, “but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.” The man serves, and notice he says, and my house. He builds them so that those children have integrity too.

sense.text:
If a sister tries to apply Proverbs 31 without genuine submission, it is not Proverbs 31. It’s not a wise woman building her house but one tearing it down, decorations for a house with a weak foundation. Soft, respectful and quiet: write that down, especially you loudmouth, disrespectful ones. Saying I’m not the only one with issues is deflection, not addressing your responsibilities. If submission depends on how he treats you, it’s not submission, it’s manipulation. It’s not your job to fix the man’s issues; stay in your lane and pray, because Christ is the head of your husband, not you. If you fear God you do what he says, and if you can’t get that part right, the fear is feigned.

Proverbs 31 shows a woman industrious and wise, a steward of the household and a support to her husband, but it is not about tasks and servitude; the submission has to come first. “A shamefaced and faithful woman is a double grace”: shamefaced and faithful, she submits regardless of anything, not conditional, not manipulation, and meditates on what submission means. “And her continent mind cannot be valued”: a mind that is not swayed, without the mood swings and all the other BS brought into the situation.

“As the sun when it ariseth in the high heaven; so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house.” Proverbs 31 falls under this, but it starts with the faithful, continent mind and the shamefacedness of submission. Order equals beauty, sisters. Wives who neglect their homes for other things are out of order and out of alignment with God’s will. The home is the first priority above all things, beginning with the husband and then the children, because of the responsibility given to the woman.
“So is the beauty of the face in ripe age.” Men age gracefully, women just age. If you want your husband to see you beautiful the rest of his days, you have to apply this.

“As the golden pillars are upon the sockets of silver; so are the fair feet with a constant heart.” That is the beauty he will see in you, past the age and past the gray hairs. None of it is physical beauty. The fair feet go into Proverbs 31, and the constant heart is not letting things pull you away from the Lord and your lord. Beauty is functional, not sexualized.

precepts.why: Read again: “A woman that honoureth her husband shall be judged wise of all; but she that dishonoureth him in her pride shall be counted ungodly of all.” The shamefaced and faithful woman, the continent mind, the ordering of her house and the constant heart are some of the ways she honours him.

“That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, to be discreet, chaste, keepers at home”: keepers at home is the ordering of her house. “good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.” It says teach them to love their husbands, and sums it up as obedient to their own husbands.

Sisters, if you are not applying this, you are blasphemous. When you sit in the judgment seat, it will not help to say my husband did this and my husband did that, so that’s why I did that. He will say, that’s blasphemy what you did.

Love the husband, love the children, keep the home: that is the biblical model of marriage, complementary responsibilities. The woman’s responsibilities may seem longer, but the man’s carry much more weight, because he is the one that is accountable.

sense.text: “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord.” As unto the Lord: the same way you submit yourself to Christ and the Most High, not less, not below it, the exact same way. That is why reverence is so much more profound than respect.

“For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.” That is a different measure of accountability and responsibility. The wife’s list looks much longer in the scriptures, and rightly so, because she has accountability to her husband and to God by being in submission to her husband. But the husband has her life on the line, the children’s lives, and for many who move for the nation, the nation behind that too, like where it says be not many masters, because of the judgment.

“Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.” Why? Because the husband is the saviour of the body, he puts his soul on the line for that measure of accountability. Sisters, your accountability is only for yourself; the husband is accountable for you, the house and the nation. Does that not deserve honour? They want to see him take a bullet or a knife for them, not seeing the higher spiritual burden he carries. That is the husband and wife that agree together: a complementary responsibility.

Marriage serves a greater purpose than companionship alone. It reflects the relationship between Christ and his people, the Israelites, us: “This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church.” Marriage was designed to show faithfulness, sacrifice and covenant, mirroring our commitment to Christ and his to us. That is the mystery, and because we refuse to embrace it, we keep having a cycle of issues.

“And the wife see that she reverence her husband.” Reverence is beyond respect. It is a profound, heartfelt attitude of awe, respect and holy fear, and it shows itself in obedience, worship and submission to authority. Not that you kneel and pray to your husband, but that is the veneration you have for him. You can’t do it as a job description; then you forget and become derelict in your duties, because it isn’t coming from genuine respect and from pleasing the Lord and your lord. You have to feel it, and pray for that spirit if you don’t have it. That is the order that makes marriages sound and strong.

Scripture doesn’t define marriage by feelings; it defines it by function. Marriage came from God; culture later made it ceremonies and a business and put unrealistic expectations on it, and the traditions don’t replace the original design. Marriage is meant to function first, and through the process of aging together the feelings do what they do.

But there will be conflict: “Nevertheless such shall have trouble in the flesh.” There will be trouble in the marriage, and how you deal with it depends on what your expectations were going into it.

precepts.why: “A virtuous woman rejoiceth her husband, and he shall fulfil the years of his life in peace.” The Bible calls for peace in the marriage: not war, not strife, not enmity, not division, not variance. The trouble in the flesh is dealt with as the wife rejoices her husband through reverence, and he stays in his integrity because there is peace in the household. Peace, not passion. Peace, not feelings.

sense.text: “Keep the ordinances, as I delivered them to you”: keep the order as it was delivered, and then comes the summary.

“The head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.” When marriage is grounded in the order God established, love becomes stronger. You have the passion and the joy; not romance, a new modern term, but the more meaningful feelings behind it, and the marriage becomes more durable over time.

There is a lot going on in the earth, and it is not enough to be aware of it; we must take urgent action. Prophecy is not entertainment, brothers and sisters. It is a sign for us to correct ourselves and set things in order, individually and as a people.
